title: NLM Training Grant Meeting R13
text:
We propose to hold a three-day T15 training grant meeting which is an essential component of
the training of our pre-doctoral trainees and post-doctoral fellows and allows them the
opportunity to present in front of their peers, to understand the breadth of the disciple of
Biomedical Informatics and Data Science at a national scope. This meeting will bring fellows
from all over the nation together for them to present their work, and use critical thinking to
review and question the methods, results and conclusions of their peers.

title: Advancing functional mass spectrometry imaging methodology to monitor dynamic physiological processes
text:
RELEVANCE TO PUBLIC HEALTH
A new functional imaging method will be developed to characterize metabolic activity variations across healthy
organs and tumor tissue. Functional imaging can be used to identify therapeutic targets in human disease.

title: Transcriptional Regulation in ZFTA-RELA Ependymoma
text:
The overall goal of this proposal is to dissect the regulation and function, of developmental transcription factors
on brain tumor development, and understand how these factors shape the microenvironment. Our studies are
important for a more complete understanding of the regulation of gene expression programs in brain cancer.

title: Tunneling Nanotube Inhibitors for Cancer Immunotherapy
text:
Despite the promise of the immune checkpoint inhibitors, the outcomes with recently approved
immunotherapies remain poor in many cancers. Less than 20% of patients treated with immune checkpoint
inhibitors show durable response. This proposal studies a novel mechanism of immune evasion by
nanotube-mediated mitochondria harvesting from immune cells by cancer cells, and will develop novel
exocyst inhibitors that can overcome this barrier that limits immune checkpoint inhibitors.

title: A novel BRET system to optimize and image in vivo recording of neural activity in freely behaving animals
text:
Title:
A novel BRET system to optimize and image in vivo recording of neural activity in
freely behaving animals
Narrative:
This project will develop new sensors and instruments for monitoring and imaging in vivo neural activity without
damage and distortion. These sensors will be an optimal partner with the revolutionary ability to control the
activity of neurons and behavior by optogenetic stimulation, thereby providing a new fundamental tool for
neurobiological research in its quest to identify new ways to treat and prevent brain disorders.

title: Mechanisms of gene expression regulation in pancreatic cancer
text:
Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a lethal cancer with a 5-year survival rate ~10% and is predicted
to become the second deadliest cancer within the next 10 years. Epigenetic changes regulating gene
expression have become a focus of intense research to help in the development of new treatment for this
dismal condition. This proposal will investigate the role of nuclear myosins in chromatin organization leading
epigenetic silencing of gene expression during PDAC transformation.

title: PhAIge Therapy Center: AI-Guided Tailspike Engineering and Molecular Typing for Rapid Phage Design and Testing Against ESKAPE Pathogens
text:
Bacteriophage therapy offers a promising alternative to antibiotics for treating multidrug-resistant Klebsiella
pneumoniae and other dangerous ESKAPE pathogens. By modernizing phage discovery with high-throughput
assays, computational modeling, and human-relevant organoid testing, this project will yield more effective,
personalized treatments. In the long term, these innovations will help reduce morbidity and mortality by
combatting antibiotic resistance on a global scale.

title: CRISPR-Cas13-based rapid HIV-1 test
text:
The proposed research is relevant to public health because it will result in the development of a user friendly,
rapid HIV self-test for detecting early stages of acute infection and viral rebound in individuals receiving
antiretroviral therapy. Thus, the proposed research is relevant to NIAID's mission by advancing HIV research
and improving human health through the development of new diagnostics tools to improve the diagnosis and
clinical management of HIV-infected individuals.

title: Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network Neuropathology Core
text: Core D: Neuropathology PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT Mounting evidence suggests Alzheimer’s disease (AD) begins decades before symptoms appear, during a preclinical phase marked by amyloid plaques, tau tangles, neuroinflammation, and progressive neuronal damage. Advances in biomarkers such as biofluid analyses and neuroimaging now allow researchers to detect and monitor these changes in living individuals. Despite these tools, AD remains poorly understood, and deeper insights are essential to accelerate the development of effective treatments. In this effort, studies and samples of postmortem brain tissue are indispensable. Comprehensive brain examination can establish not only whether a person had AD and how severe it had become, but can also detect other neuropathologies that often coincide with AD. Just as important: leveraging brain specimens can reveal new secrets about AD pathophysiology and facilitate studies that are not possible in living participants. The mission of the Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network (DIAN) Neuropathology Core (NPC) is to collect, process, analyze, store, and distribute autopsy brain tissue from affected study participants and non-affected controls to support DIAN’s scientific project and other projects around the world. Towards this end, the NPC examines brains for the amounts and distributions of neuron loss, gliosis, vascular disease sequela, and deposits of Aß, hyperphosphorylated tau, alpha-synuclein, and pTDP-43. These detailed studies enable us to provide neuropathologic diagnoses to families and to supply appropriate tissues to scientific studies. Further, by providing tissue samples and data to DIAN’s Scientific Project, the NPC will help to: (in Aim 1) improve our understanding of how various autosomal dominant AD (ADAD) mutations influence Ab production and subsequently lead to the accumulation of pathologic Ab and tau in the brain; (in Aim 2) study the effects of fibrillar tau (purified from DIAN participant AD brain samples) on proteostasis and synaptic function of neurons (grown in culture from induced pluripotent stem cells [iPSCs] derived from participant skin samples); (in Aim 3) explore how different activation states of astrocytes and microglia contribute to disease progression and the development of symptoms, determine whether brain-derived fibrillar tau can induce activation of iPSC-derived astrocytes and microglia, and evaluate whether iPSC-derived astrocytes and microglia that carry various ADAD mutations differ in their responses to fibrillar tau. Collectively, findings from these DIAN Scientific Project Aims – and from other approved external projects supported by DIAN Obs NPC tissue samples and data – will advance our understanding of AD and perhaps suggest new therapeutic strategies for clinical trials.

title: Exploration of the role of FOSL1-mediated liquid-liquid phase separation in cisplatin resistance in HNSCC
text:
Cancer continues to be a significant global health issue, with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC)
being the seventh most common cancer worldwide. While cisplatin is the predominant chemotherapy to treat
HNSCC, the development of resistance poses a significant challenge in effectively treating HNSCC patients. The
successful completion of this project will uncover the key mechanisms driving cisplatin resistance in HNSCC,
providing the foundation for developing novel drugs to overcome cisplatin resistance.

title: Understanding Clonal Enrichment and Functional Impact of HPV Integration Events in OPSCC
text:
The basic pathogenetic mechanisms of human papilloma virus positive oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma
(HPV+ OPSCC) remain incompletely understood. This proposal seeks to overcome a substantial gap in
knowledge by using our recently developed liquid biopsy technology to study the clonal evolution of HPV-
integrated tumor cells in the context of treatment failure. Furthermore, we will also evaluate the basic genetic
mechanisms by which integration impacts fusion gene formation in order to understand how structurally
independent HPV-host fusion genes drive cell state heterogeneity in HPV+ tumors.

title: CD90-targeted nanoparticles for in vivo hematopoietic stem cell gene therapy
text:
Blood stem cell gene therapy for the treatment of blood diseases and disorders is currently greatly limited by the
targeting efficiency and the number of institutions with appropriate infrastructure to perform this treatment. The
ability to safely and specifically modify blood stem cells directly in patients (in vivo) would help to increase the
feasibility and portability of gene therapy. Here, we aim to develop polymeric and lipid nanoparticle formulations
to perform gene editing in vivo and increase efficiency, reduce costs, and bring gene therapy to the patient.

title: Assessment of strategies for targeting transcriptional co-activators in colorectal cancer
text:
Colorectal cancer accounts for 8-9% of all cancer-related deaths in the U.S. in both women and men, and
estimates predict it will account for 52,550 deaths in 2023. The long-term goal for this research is to provide
novel therapeutic strategies to treat patients with metastatic disease by targeting PGC-1β signaling.
Additionally, we hope to develop treatment strategies with tolerable side effects to lengthen and improve the
quality of life after a diagnosis of metastatic colorectal cancer.

title: Progressive Multifocal Leukoenephalopathy: Endemic Viruses and Lethal Brain Disease
text:
JC virus (JCPyV) infects greater than 50% of the human population worldwide and causes a fatal
central nervous system disease in humans known as Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy or
PML in individuals with compromised immune systems. This proposal focuses on understanding the
pathophysiology of JC virus induced PML. Our work is focused on translating our significant work on
the basic biology of JCPyV infection to the clinic by the identification of biomarkers and the
identification of small compounds that can prevent or treat disease.

title: Genetics and Cell Biology Training Program
text: The proposed training program will support the training of predoctoral students in genetics and cell biology, with direct implications for human health and disease. The training includes clinically relevant coursework and research opportunities and will prepare trainees for a range of careers in the biomedical workforce.

title: Discovering human divergent activity-regulated elements using comparative, computational, and functional approaches
text:
Linking the evolution of cognitive abilities to genetic differences between humans and nonhuman primates is
challenging since it requires an understanding of how life experiences induce changes in brain activity and
neuronal gene expression. We will use experimental methods in primary and stem cell-derived neuronal cultures
to investigate how neuronal activity-responsive regulatory elements differ between humans and other primates,
and we will create machine learning models to predict the location of these elements in the genome. Since many
neurodevelopmental disorders are thought to involve disruptions in neuronal plasticity, understanding the
molecular and cellular mechanisms of plasticity in human neurons will be crucial to understanding both the
evolutionary specializations of the human brain and to developing treatments for neurological disorders.

title: The Development of Tabletop Brain-Mapping Platform
text:
This Phase II proposal describes the development of an automated whole-brain mapping
platform. It images and sections whole mouse brains into a series of thin sections automatically
mounted on glass slides indexed to their correct location within the 3D brain. It offers wide
compatibility with advanced Spatial Biology techniques and existing histology methods
including classical CNS and neurodegenerative markers and immunohistochemistry protocols.
The device has an integrated brain mapping software platform that allows individual research
labs to conduct whole brain mapping studies without the need for specialized equipment or
personnel.

title: Northeast Node of the National Drug Abuse Treatment Clinical Trials Network
text:
The proposed activities of the Northeast Node of the National Drug Abuse Treatment Clinical Trials Network
(CTN) reflect a vision for the next iteration of the CTN in the next 7 years. Overall, the Northeast Node will
focus on identifying the most significant and timely substance use needs in our communities, leading and
partnering on rigorous and innovative research projects to tackle these challenges, and scaling-up and
sustaining best practices in our nation.

title: The genetic basis of emerging multidrug resistance in Plasmodium falciparum African malaria
text:
This research will implement and characterize genetic crosses to identify key molecular determinants associated
with artemisinin resistance and reduced lumefantrine susceptibility in African Plasmodium falciparum malaria
parasites and characterize the impact of these mutations on parasite fitness and transmission. The results will
provide robust molecular markers that can be used for molecular surveillance of parasites resistant to this first-
line drug in Africa, where the disease burden is by far the greatest in the world. Our findings will help guide
strategies to protect artemisinin-based combination therapies, impede the spread and establishment of multidrug
resistance, and inform strategies to design more effective antimalarial drug treatments aimed at reducing
malaria’s massive impact on global health.

title: Harnessing Myeloid Olfactory Receptors to Reprogram Tumor Immunity
text:
The sense of smell is not confined solely to the nose; immune cells known as monocytes and macrophages also
express functional olfactory receptors (ORs) capable of detecting and responding to metabolites produced by
tumors. This project will explore how these receptors reprogram tumor-associated macrophages in melanoma,
assess their predictive value for immunotherapy success, and pharmacologically target ORs to activate
macrophage anti-tumor function. By harnessing this newly discovered macrophage sensing pathway, we aim to
make checkpoint therapies work for more patients and improve survival.
